Fragmenta ex commentariis in Proverbia
ΕΚ ΤΩΝ ΩΡΙΓΕΝΟΥΣ ΕΙΣ ΤΑΣ ΠΑΡΟΙΜΙΑΣ ΣΟΛΟΜΩΝΤΟΣ.
13.17 ΚΕΦ. Αʹ.
Παροιμίαι Σολομῶντος υἱοῦ ∆αυΐδ. Υἱὸς ∆αυῒδ καὶ ὁ Σωτὴρ λέγεται. Οὗτος
εἰρηνικὸς ἡμῶν Σωτὴρ ὁ γενόμενος ἐκ σπέρματος ∆αυῒδ, τὸ κατὰ σάρκα,
ἐβασίλευσεν ἐν Ἰσραήλ. ∆ιὸ καὶ ἐπεγράφη τὴν ὑπὲρ ἀνθρώπων οἰκονομίαν τελῶν·
Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ βασι λεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων. Ἰουδαῖοί εἰσιν, ὁ Ἰσραὴλ, ὧνεἰρηνικὸς
Σωτὴρ βασιλεύει ὡς διορατικῶν, ἐὰν ὦσιν ἀληθῶς Ἰσραήλ. Οὐ γὰρ ὅσοι σπέρμα τοῦ
Ἀβραὰμ, πάντως καὶ τέκνα, τῷ μὴ ποιεῖν τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Ἀβραάμ. Τοῦ γνῶναι σοφίαν
καὶ παιδείαν. Σοφία ἐστὶν ἐπιστήμη θείων καὶ ἀνθρωπίνων πραγμάτων κατά 13.20
ληψις· κατὰ δέ τινας, ἀτμίς ἐστι τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ δυ νάμεως, καὶ ἀπόῤῥοια τῆς τοῦ
Παντοκράτορος δόξης εἰλικρινής· οὐδὲν γὰρ εἰς αὐτὴν σκοτεινὸν ἐμπίπτει·
ἀπαύγασμα γάρ ἐστι φωτὸς ἀϊδίου, καὶ ἔσοπτρον ἀκηλίδωτον τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ
ἐνεργείας, καὶ εἰκὼν τῆς ἀγαθότητος αὐτοῦ. Ὁ γινώσκων ἔρ
pass_a_gloss: Fragments from the commentaries on Proverbs. From the things of Origen into the Proverbs of Solomon. Chapter 1, PG 13.17. Proverbs of Solomon son of David. Son of David the Savior also is called. This peaceable Savior of ours who came to be from David seed according to the flesh reigned in Israel. Therefore he was also inscribed, as he completed the economy on behalf of humans: This is the King of the Jews. Jews are Israel, over whom the peaceable Savior reigns as over discerning ones, if they are truly Israel. For not as many as are seed of Abraham are in every way also children, by not doing the works of Abraham. To know wisdom and training. Wisdom is knowledge of divine and human affairs — a taking-hold; and according to some, it is a vapor of the power of God, and a pure outflow of the glory of the Almighty; for nothing dark falls into it; for it is a radiance of everlasting light, and a spotless mirror of the activity of God, and an image of his goodness. The one who knows works of wisdom knows these things, that is, the radiance of the everlasting, and the spotless mirror of God activity, and the image of his goodness. And these things are nothing other than to know the Son of the love of God, and the wisdom, the Christ. For Christ is power of God and wisdom of God. And this is not revealed from flesh and blood, but from the heavenly Father. And the one who knows the science of the divine oracles — legal and prophetic, gospel and apostolic — also knows wisdom. He sets the foundation upon the rock, that is upon the faith of Christ, so as to hold out against rains and winds and spirits, namely the temptations that come from wherever. And if Luke says that he praised the steward of injustice, he used the word in a stretched sense, taking the praise upon the shrewdness, and through the sharpness of mind; which seems also to be shown in And the serpent was shrewdest of all the beasts, according to which it has also been said, Become shrewd as the serpent — as if not inexperienced of the serpent craftinesses. He will also understand a parable and a dark saying, and sayings of wise men and riddles. Let us observe what difference these have toward one another; and first let us see what a parable ever is, from the gospel starting-points we have. For others also used the name of parable, and Matthew thus: On that day, going out from the house, Jesus sat beside the sea, and the whole crowd stood upon the shore, and he spoke to them many things in parables: Look, the sower went out to sow. A parable, then, is a speech as concerning something that has come to be, which has not come to be according to the letter, yet is able to come to be, figuratively indicative of affairs by transfer of the things said in the parable. For according to the wording there has not come to be The sower went out, as we say the things of history have come to be; yet it is possible for it to come to be according to the letter: Look, the sower went out, and so on. I myself, however, think that Jesus, speaking in parables to those outside — to whom, because they are outside, it had not been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God — has gone out of the house, as Matthew recorded, not without cause and reason when he made On that day, going out of the house, Jesus sat beside the sea. For it was fitting, toward those who did not have room to enter into the house themselves but were outside it, that he go out of it. And that Matthew has understood something of this sort at the place will be clear to the one who has watched what is brought on: for leaving the crowds, he says, he entered into his house, and to the disciples he uncovers the things of the parable. Keep watch in these things in what manner Jesus speaks to the crowds in parables, and without a parable speaks nothing to them; which he also does even to the present; for the crowds do not have room for interpretation of parables. And attend also to Leaving the crowds he entered into his own house,
pass_b_english: Fragments from the commentaries on Proverbs. From Origen on the Proverbs of Solomon. Chapter 1.

Proverbs of Solomon, son of David. The Savior too is called son of David. This peaceable Savior of ours, who came from David seed according to the flesh, reigned in Israel. That is why, as he completed the economy for human beings, he was also labeled: This is the King of the Jews. Jews are Israel — those over whom the peaceable Savior reigns as over people who see clearly — if they are truly Israel. For not all who are Abraham seed are also children, when they do not do Abraham works.

To know wisdom and training. Wisdom is knowledge that takes hold of divine and human affairs. Some say it is a vapor of God power and a pure outflow of the Almighty glory; nothing dark falls into it. It is a radiance of everlasting light, a spotless mirror of God working, and an image of his goodness. Whoever knows wisdom works knows these: that radiance, that spotless mirror, that image of goodness. And that is nothing other than to know the Son of God love, and the Wisdom who is Christ. For Christ is God power and God wisdom. This is not unveiled from flesh and blood, but from the heavenly Father. Whoever also knows the science of the divine oracles — of the Law and the prophets, of the Gospels and the apostles — knows wisdom.

He sets the foundation on the rock, that is on faith in Christ, so that it can hold against rains and winds and spirits — against temptations from whatever quarter. And if Luke says he praised the steward of injustice, he stretched the word, taking the praise for shrewdness and for sharpness of mind. That seems to show also in the serpent was shrewdest of all the beasts, and in the saying be shrewd as serpents — as if not inexperienced in the serpent tricks.

He will also understand a parable and a dark saying, sayings of the wise and riddles. Let us see how these differ. First, what is a parable, from the Gospel materials we have? Others used the name, and Matthew writes: On that day Jesus went out of the house, sat beside the sea, and the whole crowd stood on the shore, and he spoke many things to them in parables: Look, a sower went out to sow. A parable, then, is speech as about something that happened, which did not happen according to the letter yet could happen, and which points figuratively to realities by transferring what the parable says. For the sower went out did not happen as history happens; yet it could happen according to the letter.

I think that when Jesus speaks in parables to those outside — to whom, being outside, it was not given to know the mysteries of God kingdom — he has gone out of the house, as Matthew reports, and not without reason when he writes that on that day Jesus went out of the house and sat beside the sea. Toward those who could not enter the house but stood outside it, it was fitting that he go out. That Matthew intends this is clear from what follows: leaving the crowds, he entered his house and opens the parable to the disciples. Watch how he speaks to the crowds in parables and says nothing to them without a parable — as he still does, for crowds cannot take an interpretation of parables. Attend also to Leaving the crowds, he entered his own house,
